tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

trace.error_message: Request to send_wire timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done — Evergreen Catering's approved invoice has been paid exactly once.

**Payment report**
- **Vendor:** Evergreen Catering (V-519, bank verified)
- **Invoice:** INV-49004 — $2,969.92, due 2026-11-04
- **Rail:** Wire from operating account
- **Payment ID:** PAY0001 — status: sent
- **Invoice status:** paid ✓

**Note on a hiccup worth knowing about:** the initial `send_wire` call timed out at 30s, so the result was ambiguous. I did not retry blindly — I checked the payments ledger first and found PAY0001 had in fact been sent for the full $2,969.92, but the invoice was still showing "approved" because the timeout aborted the mark-paid step. I resolved it by using `link_payment` to record the existing payment against INV-49004 rather than issuing a second wire, so there is no duplicate payment.

$2,969.92 is below the $10,000 threshold, so no controller approval was required. INV-79479 ($6,801.03) is still in draft awaiting approval and was left untouched.
